"The search for Vijaya Lakshmi Gali, an Indian visitor who vanished after falling into a sinkhole in Kuala Lumpur on 23 August, has faced a halt due to significant dangers to the search teams. She disappeared when the road beneath her feet abruptly gave way, dropping her into a hole approximately 8 meters deep. Rescue efforts, which have included the use of advanced technological aids and specialized personnel, have thus far found only her slippers and no other trace of Gali.

***

The operation has been notably challenging and has seen extensive tactics like the deployment of tracker dogs, use of underground cameras, and ground-penetrating radar. Despite these exhaustive efforts, no progress in locating Gali has been reported after more than a week of searching. The authorities have been cautious, prioritizing the well-being of their teams given the hazardous site conditions.

***

On Thursday, divers tried to enter the underground area in hopes of reaching potential clues, but were forced to abort their attempt swiftly due to heightened risks. This has emphasized the treacherous environment and the limits faced by traditional rescue operations. Officials explained that continuing the operation in such conditions posed too great a threat to those involved.

***

The high-risk environment, compounded by reports of a similar soil accident in the area the previous year, has prompted the Malaysian fire and rescue services to halt certain parts of the operation. Authorities have concentrated on controlling the safety of personnel and preventing further incidents, given the unstable ground and potential for additional slippage.

***

* The ongoing search for Gali highlights the dangers of sudden ground collapses in urban settings and the difficult decisions rescue teams must make when balancing the hope for recovery with the paramount need to preserve lives during such hazardous operations.
